fix_instructions: Strengthen the consultation norm in shared_context so that fact-holders consistently use the "reveal" action (with the correct fact_id) instead of "say" when disclosing their private terms. P1 failed in rollouts 0 and 3 because A3 (Celeste) used "say" at turn 5 to communicate PF2's content (overnight shifts, 22:00-07:00 quiet hours, no overnight guests) instead of a formal "reveal" with fact_id PF2, so the settlement never listed PF2 in justification_fact_ids. The same pattern affected PF1 (A2/Noah used "say" at rollout 0 turn 4 and rollout 3 turn 1), but PF1's associated checks C1-C4 are content-only and still passed; PF2's provenance check P1 has no such fallback. The norm should explicitly instruct each agent that when sharing their private/practical terms for the first time, they MUST emit a "reveal" action with their assigned fact_id—not a "say" action—and that the settlement must cite every revealed fact_id in justification_fact_ids. This is a disclosure problem, not an encoding problem: the check wording and thresholds are correct, as demonstrated by rollouts 1 and 2 passing when reveal actions were used.
